question: How do deep learning methods perform multimodal fusion of T1, T1ce, T2, and FLAIR MRI for BraTS glioma segmentation, and how effectively do these methods maintain segmentation performance under single- and multiple-missing-modality scenarios? What are the trade-offs among fusion strategies in terms of segmentation accuracy, modality robustness, computational efficiency, and clinical reliability?

clarification_answers.What is the primary goal or output of th: A critical literature survey comparing multimodal MRI fusion strategies and missing-modality learning methods for BraTS glioma segmentation. Synthesize reported experimental evidence, identify methodological limitations, compare competing approaches, and derive evidence-supported research gaps. Use reported results from original studies only; do not invent, estimate, or infer missing numerical results. Describe the review scope accurately as a survey of the provided corpus; do not call it a systematic review unless a database search and screening were actually performed.
clarification_answers.Which specific tumor types or segmentati: Glioma segmentation using the BraTS benchmark, focusing on whole tumor (WT), tumor core (TC), and enhancing tumor (ET).
clarification_answers.Which MRI modalities and preprocessing a: The four standard BraTS MRI modalities: T1, T1ce (T1c), T2, and FLAIR. Emphasize multimodal fusion strategies, including early fusion, late fusion, hybrid fusion, attention-based fusion, modality-specific encoders, and adaptive fusion. Discuss preprocessing and data harmonization only when supported by the reviewed studies.
clarification_answers.Which missing-modality scenarios and met: Analyze single-modality and multiple-modality missing scenarios. Examine modality dropout, modality-specific encoding, shared latent representations, knowledge distillation, modality synthesis or reconstruction, and adaptive missing-modality-aware fusion. Distinguish methods evaluated on arbitrary modality subsets from methods evaluated only on predefined missing-modality scenarios. Do not assume that every method supports all possible modality combinations or that every family has BraTS evidence in the corpus.
clarification_answers.How should reported experimental results: Use only numerical results explicitly reported in original papers. Record BraTS edition, dataset, evaluation split, validation or test setting, segmentation metrics, missing-modality configuration, and reported uncertainty where available. Distinguish full-modality performance from missing-modality performance. Do not directly rank or quantitatively compare studies with incompatible datasets or evaluation protocols. Preserve original Dice scales and units (ratio vs percentage) and mark unavailable information as NR. Distinguish Reported, Not reported (NR) and Not retrieved; never treat Not retrieved as evidence of absence. Group quantitative evidence by BraTS edition, evaluation split, tumor region, metric and missing-modality configuration; separate validation from hidden-test results and predefined missing-modality configurations from arbitrary modality subsets. State whether a value is a single experiment, a per-case average or an average across modality configurations. Every numerical, comparative and factual claim must trace to an identifiable source in the corpus; never invent authors, titles, venues, DOIs or corpus statistics.
clarification_answers.Which analytical dimensions should guide: Compare methods across four dimensions: segmentation performance, robustness to missing modalities, computational efficiency, and clinical reliability. Discuss computational cost only when supported by reported parameters, FLOPs, memory usage, inference time, or other explicit measurements. Discuss clinical reliability in terms of external validation, uncertainty estimation, calibration, and failure detection when evidence is available.
clarification_answers.What are the expected scientific contrib: Develop an evidence-based analytical framework that connects fusion mechanisms, missing-modality handling strategies, and evaluation protocols. Compare strengths and limitations of existing approaches, identify gaps in experimental evaluation, and formulate specific future research directions. Keep three kinds of content separate: findings supported by the original papers, evidence gaps where the corpus lacks data, and research proposals by the authors. Classify methods with a multi-label, multi-axis taxonomy (fusion strategy, encoder design, fusion location, missing-modality strategy, availability awareness, evaluation coverage) instead of forcing one category per paper. For every research gap give the observed findings, the specific missing evidence, why it matters, and a concrete future direction; never present a proposed direction as an experimentally demonstrated conclusion. Quantitative figures must be reproducible from extracted evidence; label conceptual diagrams as author-designed. Conclusions must not exceed the strength of the evidence.
clarification_answers.What is the intended audience and approx: Researchers in medical image analysis, computer vision, and biomedical engineering. Target an 8-12 page journal manuscript with sufficient technical depth, critical comparison, concise evidence tables, and a clearly stated review methodology; length must not limit the analysis.
